content:
jordan: Heads up — us-central1 preemptible GPU turbulence starting ~06:12 UTC. cluster-autoscaler lagging, pods pending ~450s. noticed big kubelet churn and some NAT errors.
mei: Can you paste the recent pod list / node status?
jordan: sure, gist of output:
```
NAMESPACE   NAME                        STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference   trainer-abc-0               Pending   0          8m
inference   worker-xyz-1                Pending   0          9m

kubectl describe nodes | grep -E "NotReady|Preempted|taint" -A2
# shows nodes NotReady -> Kubelet lost + cloud preempted events
```
carl: Is this pure preemption or something else stepping on the nodes? SNAT pool exhaustion previously made kube-proxy flake and extended termination.
jordan: Both. Cloud preemptions spiking and we hit NAT ephemeral port limits in the cluster egress path; node controller then spent ~60s trying to update status, CA started deleting then recreating -> thrash.
ryan: Can we bias CA to prefer spinning non-preemptible replicas in the impacted zones temporarily? cost-wise that's heavy.
carl: quick numbers: non-preemptible GPU ~4.2x on-demand cost vs preemptible. But if we avoid SLA breaches it's worth a few hours.
capacity-bot: ALERT: gpu-p100-spot eviction rate 18% (15m avg). reserve pool 'reserve-gpu-buffer' has 6 available nodes.
mei: Proposed immediate actions: 1) scale up reserve-gpu-buffer, 2) cordon/drain oldest preemptible nodes to reduce reclaim-induced kills, 3) increase CA stabilization windows, 4) temporary CA expander to "least-waste".
jordan: I can push the CA expander change and bump reserve pool. plan: patch CA configmap ->
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler --type merge -p '{"data":{"expander":"least-waste"}}'
# then kubectl scale nodepool reserve-gpu-buffer --replicas=18
```
ryan: Also check taint/toleration mismatch — a few critical services didn't tolerate the 'preemptible=true' taint so they stayed pending even when reserve nodes came up.
carl: I'll scan deployments for tolerations and add quick fixes.
mei: Finance FYI: shifting ~30% of latency-sensitive work to dedicated instances temporarily estimated +$1.1k/hr. @jordan please flag if we escalate.
jordan: Rolled: reserve-gpu-buffer 6 -> 18 requested. Status: 12 ready, 6 provisioning. Changed CA expander. cordoned 8 oldest preemptible nodes and draining in waves.
capacity-bot: UPDATE: eviction rate down to 4% after reserve pool scale-up.
ryan: Good. Follow-up items: write runbook entry "preemptible turbulence" covering NAT port sizing, CA knobs (stabilization window, expander), reserve pool thresholds, and cost rollback steps.
carl: I'll open a PR with runbook + terraform change to bump reserve-gpu-buffer min size by 30% for peak hours.
mei: We should also add an alert for SNAT saturation in the infra dashboards; that was the hidden multiplier here.
jordan: Agreed. I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and revert CA changes if steady. Thanks all :thumbsup:
